instruction:
Add a repo-hygiene rule: no tracked source file may contain a user-specific home path. A test will scan every tracked `.py`, `.pyi`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`, `.cfg` and `.ini` file (skipping anything under `docs/`, `.docs/` or `.claude/`, and `uv.lock`) for Windows user-home paths (`C:/Users/<name>` or `C:\Users\<name>`), Linux `/home/<name>` and macOS `/Users/<name>`, and fail on any match, including matches in comments and docstrings.

Find every such path in the tracked source and replace it with a generic placeholder: an environment-variable placeholder such as `${LUTHI_PATH}` for a local checkout, or a `/path/to/...` style example in usage text. If a literal really must stay, the line can end with `# pragma: allow-hardcoded-path`, but don't use that to avoid fixing ordinary examples.

source.subject: add path-hygiene test, genericize machine-specific path examples
